title: Lesson 16: The Crowning Gem (Advanced Division)
subtopics: Single Figure on the Flag Division
Negative Flag Digits with Bar Numbers
learningGoals: Use one-line division by two-figure divisors.
Handle advanced division with flag and bar digits.
coreIdeas: Teach one visual pattern at a time, then checkpoint immediately.
Use active recall: student states next step before final answer.
Keep board, voice, and feedback in one continuous loop.

workedExamples.question: Demo 1: Single Figure on the Flag Division
workedExamples.method: I do -> We do -> You do
workedExamples.answer: Solved with board explanation, then student teach-back.

workedExamples.question: Demo 2: Longer Number Division
workedExamples.answer: Solved mentally and verified with a quick check step.

starterPractice: Warm-up: one easy question on Single Figure on the Flag Division.
Guided: one medium question on Longer Number Division.
Independent: one challenge question on Decimalising the Remainder.

onboarding.coachIntro: Raj checks language comfort, current confidence, and session goal before starting The Crowning Gem (Advanced Division).
onboarding.placementRule: Recommended start level for Lesson 16: confident. If the learner struggles twice in one step, keep the pace slow and repeat the pattern with a smaller number.

mission.missionPromise: Use one-line division by two-figure divisors.
mission.successCelebration: Celebrate each correct step in The Crowning Gem (Advanced Division) with points, a badge pulse, and a quick coach line before moving on.

microLessonPattern: Coach opens with one short hook and names the pattern.
Coach models one worked move on the board.
Coach reads the exercise question aloud.
Niagh tries before the full answer is shown.
Instant feedback either celebrates or repairs the first mistake.
A quick review prompt decides whether the learner advances or repeats.

rewardLoop.xpUnit: Award 10 to 20 XP per exercise group based on the step position in the lesson path.
rewardLoop.streakRule: Keep the streak visible on every step and protect it with immediate retries instead of long explanations.
rewardLoop.badgeRule: Each exercise group has one badge focus tied to the subtopic being learned.
rewardLoop.celebrationStyle: Short praise, points pulse, and progress-bar movement after every correct response.

reviewLoop.trigger: If the learner answers incorrectly, hesitates, or shows low confidence, reopen the same pattern with one smaller follow-up.
reviewLoop.practiceStyle: Use the micro-practice line as the first repair loop before advancing.
reviewLoop.masteryRule: Advance only after the learner can answer the checkpoint and complete one try in the same subtopic.
reviewLoop.revisitRule: Weak steps should return in the next session as review cards before new content.

uiDirectives.noScrollGoal: The learner should see mission progress, the current question, and the main action buttons without long vertical scrolling.

teachingFlowStages.intent: Set context: the flag method divides by any two-digit number in one line — no long-division columns.
Explain: split divisor into flag digit (units) and stem. Divide by stem, subtract flag*quotient-digit for remainder.
Teacher demonstrates: 135/11. Stem=1, flag=1. 13/1=13->Q digit 1, rem=3. 35-1*1=25. 25/1->Q=2 R=3. Answer: 12 R 3.
Student divides 156/12 with tutor scaffolding each flag subtraction.
Student independently uses flag division for 3-digit by 2-digit problems.
Tutor gives step-by-step correction logic and shows where the student's reasoning went wrong.
Explicit learner-response gate: student confirms understanding before tutor advances to the next subtopic.
